newsitem.title: UK: NWE gasoline trims gains in active barge trading.
newsitem.headline: NWE gasoline trims gains in active barge trading.

text.p: NWE gasoline prices trimmed their gains after crude pulled back from its daily highs and NYMEX gasoline fell sharply, traders said on Monday.
But prices still showed gains of $5-$6 on signs of heavy buying in the ARA barge market that may be tied to stockbuilding ahead of the U.K. budget on November 26, they said.

In addition, the arbitrage to the U.S. opened late last week and traders said at least 100,000 tonnes of premium unleaded and regular unleaded was fixed for delivery this month, tightening supplies in NWE.
Traders said it appeared the arbitrage was now shut.
One broker said Eurograde barges traded as high as $231.50 and as low as $226, with anywhere from seven to 10 barge trades between the two levels.
Eurograde barges ended at $224/$227 fob ARA versus $218/$220 on Friday. Regular unleaded trading was thinner and held at a $10 discount at $214/$216, traders said.
Premium unleaded cargoes gained $5 to $230/$232 cif and regular unleaded cargoes ended at $220/$222 cif.
